claim_en: The call protocol: calling precedes every divine speaking from the tent (binyan av from the bush and Sinai), extended to all speakings, sayings, and commandings; each call the doubled name, answered 'Here I am.'
middah: I3 (the call before every speaking built from two exemplars, the bush and Sinai — the building principle; the doubled name, E10, beside)

claim_en: Single receiver, bounded broadcast: Aaron, elders, sons, and angels excluded ('to him'); the voice cut off at the tent boundary though mighty; source address between the two cherubs.
middah: E2 ('to him' excludes Aaron, the elders, the sons, the angels; the voice cut at the tent's boundary)

claim_en: The paragraph-channel charter: the pauses received no call and exist 'to give time for reflection between section and section' — the tradition's own account of the scroll's paragraph breaks.
middah: ink (the paragraph breaks themselves — the tradition's account of the scroll's pauses as time for reflection)

claim_en: Caller domain: proselytes in, heretics out (include-then-exclude on covenant-acceptance); offering optional; sanctify-by-declaration first; korban always paired with the Tetragrammaton (scannable ink invariant).
middah: E1 (proselytes included then heretics excluded on covenant-acceptance — include-then-exclude; the offering-and-Name pairing an ink invariant)

source: Sifra, Vayikra Dibbura DeNedavah, Section 2 6-11 + Chapter 3
claim_en: Input filter: domesticated only; excluded — the sodomy pair, the worshipped, the designated, the treifah, and the goring killer ox (Exodus 21 cross-link); partnership and communal-gift arity.
middah: E2 (domesticated only — the species words exclude the paired, the worshipped, the designated, the torn, the killer ox)

source: Sifra, Vayikra Dibbura DeNedavah, Section 3 12-15 + Chapter 5 5; Onkelos Lev 1:3
claim_en: Acceptance gate: tamim as predicate + inspection; owner transports (no delegation); the remiss vower compelled; caller-layer eligibility vs object-layer processing split (R. Chiyya).
middah: plain (the acceptance gate — unblemished as predicate, the owner transports, the remiss vower compelled; R. Chiyya's caller-layer split)
